title: Meshtastic Logistics Metadata Collector: Open-Source Software for Measuring the Operational Autonomy of SME Logistics over LoRa Mesh Networks
description:
Python software for a private Meshtastic LoRa mesh network used as a backup channel for critical logistics operations of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). It accompanies the manuscript Strengthening Operational Autonomy in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Logistics with Meshtastic Mesh Networks: Reference Architecture and Ex-Ante Model-Based Assessment and defines how the quantities predicted by that model would be recorded and computed in a field experiment.

Evidence status: no experiment has been performed with this software. It has never been connected to a Meshtastic radio and has been run only on an invented replay log in which radio values are pseudo-random or hand-set constants and event outcomes are scripted. No number produced by this package is a measurement, and none confirms any value in the accompanying article, whose numbers are ex-ante model predictions obtained with separate scripts. Every result of kpi.py carries a provenance block that marks generated input as "not a measurement".

  • collector.py – gateway collector (USB/TCP, untested on hardware, or offline replay) that stores packet, device and logistics-event metadata in a local SQLite database and registers the data origin of every run;
  • logi_proto.py – 24-byte binary frame with CRC-16/CCITT for EVENT/ACCEPT/DONE/REJECT messages on PRIVATE_APP (port 256);
  • kpi.py – channel utilisation and relay airtime as reported by nodes, position delivery ratio, age of information, on-time completion of delivered critical events (upper bound of efficacy η), operational autonomy Aop and its loss-weighted form, each with sample size and 95 % interval;
  • make_replay.py, import_plan.py, run_demo.sh, tests/ – deterministic software check on generated input;
  • notebooks/meshtastic_logistics_analysis.ipynb – walk-through that reproduces the airtime column of Table A2 and checks the algebra of Equation (3).

Version 1.1.0 renames and redefines several indicators; see CHANGELOG.md. Known limitations are listed in README.md.
